content.title: About
content.content: Fruit punch is a refreshing alcoholic beverage made from a blend of fruit juices, sugar, and spirits (usually vodka or rum). It has a bright fruit aroma, a sweet‑tart taste, and a moderate alcohol strength, typically 10–15% ABV.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Historically, punch was created in colonial regions using local fruits and sugar syrup.
There are countless variations: berry, tropical, citrus, or spiced with exotic herbs.
In some countries punch is served at “punch bars,” where guests can customize their drink.
Alcoholic punch is often used as a base for cocktails and dessert sauces.

items.title: Vitamins and Antioxidants
items.content: The fruit juices in punch provide vitamin C and other antioxidants that support the immune system.

items.title: Mood Enhancement
items.content: Moderate alcohol consumption can promote relaxation and improve mood.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The water content of the juices helps maintain hydration, especially in warm weather.

items.title: Alcohol
items.content: Excessive intake can lead to intoxication, liver damage, and other health issues.

items.title: Sugar
items.content: High sugar levels increase the risk of cavities, weight gain, and blood‑glucose spikes.

items.title: Allergy to Ingredients
items.content: Some fruit juices may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Drink
content.content: Serve the punch chilled in glasses or tumblers over ice. Garnish with fruit slices, mint, or berries. For a lighter version, top with sparkling water.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared punch in a sealed bottle in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. Store individual ingredients (juice, spirit) in a cool, dark place for longer shelf life.
